questions.worked_solution:
The $4$th row of the given matrix contains two zeros, more than any other row. So, using a Laplace expansion along the $4$th row, we have   

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot {C}_{41}+0\cdot {C}_{42}+0\cdot {C}_{43}+3\cdot {C}_{44} \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{4+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}|+3\cdot (-1)^{4+4}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}|+3|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the first $3\times 3$  determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =(-1)\cdot {C}_{21}+2\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{23} \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{2+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|+2\cdot (-1)^{2+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|+2|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2-3)+2(1-3) \\  & =-5+2\cdot (-2) \\  & =-9\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute the second $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along its $3$rd row:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{31}+1\cdot {C}_{32}+1\cdot {C}_{33} \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|+1\cdot (-1)^{3+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(4-2)+(-2+1) \\  & =-2+(-1) \\  & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}|=-2\cdot (-9)+3\cdot (-3)=18-9=9.
$$

questions.problem:
Compute the following determinant using a cofactor expansion along the $2$nd row:

$$
|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 5 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using cofactor expansion along the $2$nd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 5 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{21}+0\cdot {C}_{22}+7\cdot {C}_{23}+0\cdot {C}_{24} \\  & =7\cdot (-1)^{2+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-7|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}| & =1\cdot {C}_{21}+0\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{23} \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)|\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)(-12) \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 5 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|=-7\cdot 12=-84.
$$

\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 4 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| & =(-2)\cdot {C}_{13}+0\cdot {C}_{23}+0\cdot {C}_{33}+1\cdot {C}_{43} \\  & =(-2)\cdot (-1)^{1+3}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 1 \\ -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}|+1\cdot (-1)^{4+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 1 \\ -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}|-|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
